# Judith Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_014_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Judith addressed them: "Listen to me, brothers. Take this head and hang it on the parapet of your wall.

**2** The moment dawn breaks and the sun comes up, every man arms himself and marches out — every last able-bodied man in the city. Put a commander over them. Make it look like you're going down to the plain to engage the Assyrian advance guard. But don't go down.

**3** The Assyrians will grab their weapons and pour into their camp to rouse their officers. They'll run to Holofernes' tent — and they won't find him. Panic will sweep through them and they'll run from you.

**4** Then you and every man in Israel will go after them. Cut them down where they stand.

**5** But before any of that — bring me Achior the Ammonite. Let him see and recognize the man who scorned the house of Israel and sent him to us as good as dead."

**6** They brought Achior from the house of Uzziah. He walked in. He saw the head of Holofernes — held up in the hand of one of the men standing in the assembly. And he dropped to the ground. His spirit left him.

**7** They brought him around. And the first thing he did was fall at Judith's feet and bow his face to the floor before her. Then he spoke: "Blessed are you in every tent of Judah. In every nation on earth, everyone who hears your name will be struck with awe.

**8** Now tell me — tell me everything you did." And there, in front of all the people, Judith told him everything. When she finished, the crowd erupted with a roar of joy that rang through the whole city.

**9** Achior had seen with his own eyes what the God of Israel had done. He believed — deeply, completely. He was circumcised. And he became part of the house of Israel. And so it has remained to this day.

**10** At first light, they hung the head of Holofernes on the wall. Every man armed himself. They marched out in columns toward the mountain slopes.

**11** The Assyrians spotted them. Word went up the chain of command — to the commanders, the generals, the captains, all the officers.

**12** They came to Holofernes' tent. "Wake our master," they told the man who ran all his affairs. "Those slaves have had the nerve to come down against us for battle — they're marching to their own deaths."

**13** Bagoas went in and knocked on the door of the tent. He assumed Holofernes was sleeping with Judith.

**14** No answer. He pushed the door open. He walked into the bedchamber.

And there he was — thrown on the threshold. Dead. Without his head.

**15** Bagoas let out a scream. He wept. He groaned. He kept shouting. He tore his clothes apart.

**16** He ran into the tent where Judith had been staying. She was gone. He ran back out to the troops, screaming:

**17** "Treachery! One Hebrew woman — one woman — has shamed the entire house of King Nebuchadnezzar! Holofernes is on the ground — and his head is gone!"

**18** When the officers of the Assyrian army heard this, they tore their clothes. A terror came over them unlike anything they had felt. Through the whole camp — screaming, chaos, a great and terrible roar.

**19** And in tent after tent, as the news spread, every man was struck with horror at what had happened.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Verse 14 is given maximum space — broken into four short sentences to let the discovery land with its full weight. The detail "on the threshold" is not accidental; it means his body was not carried to his bed after being rolled off. He is found where Judith left him — crumpled at the door. Verse 9 is the theological hinge: Achior, the Ammonite who spoke truth to power in ch. 5-6, now completes his journey. He said Israel could not be defeated unless they sinned against God. He was vindicated. Now he joins them.*
